title: prefill backpressure fallthrough smoother and decode jitter mitigation plan
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background:
We have observed intermittent latency regressions on short-to-medium prefill requests when the runtime falls back between FlashAttention v2 and v3 variants under input-shape and memory-pressure transitions. Symptoms include decode jitter (spikes in single-request p95) and a small amplification of tail latency during bursts. Existing kernel selection heuristics aggressively flip to v3 for large head counts / long-key workloads but oscillate for workloads near thresholds, causing workspace reallocation and prefill backpressure.

Goal:
Design a conservative smoothing layer ("fallthrough smoother") around kernel fallbacks and add a prefill backpressure hysteresis policy that reduces oscillation. Validate by microbench and production canary with metrics: p50/p95 latency, average tokens/sec, workspace alloc churn, and error rates. The target is to reduce p95 decode jitter by 40% on affected workload classes while keeping p50 within 5% of baseline and not increasing cost by >3%.

Acceptance criteria:
- New smoother reduces kernel switch frequency for same-request lifetimes by >=60% in synthetic oscillation tests.
- Production canary shows p95 decode jitter reduction >=40% for short prefills (<=64 tokens) and no degradation for long-context flows (>2048 tokens).
- Telemetry shows workspace reallocs per-minute down by >=30% on canaries.
- Rollout plan with automatic rollback on CPU/GPU OOM rate increase >0.1% or downstream error rate increase >0.05%.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Kernel Smoother: implement a lightweight in-memory state machine per-worker that tracks recent kernel choices per-model-shape fingerprint. Add exponential decay counters and a minimum-stay time window (initially 3s) to avoid immediate fallthroughs. Parameterize via runtime flags for experiments.
2) Prefill Backpressure Hysteresis: when memory pressure or workspace budget is near threshold, prefer conservative kernel variants and apply token-level pacing for prefill requests (micro-delay up to 4ms, configurable). Introduce a backpressure score combining free-workspace ratio and recent alloc churn.
3) Telemetry & Alerts: add metrics: kernel_switches.count, kernel_stability.score, prefill_backpressure.score, workspace_allocs.rate. Hook alerts to canary thresholds.
4) Microbench harness: add new attn-smoke-suite cases (short prefills 8/32/64 tokens, medium 128/256, long 1k/2k) that artificially oscillate memory pressure to stress heuristics. Capture per-step kernel choice trace and workspace usage.
5) Canary & Rollout: small traffic canary (5% of small-prefill traffic) → ramp to 25% if stable for 4h → 100% for small-prefill class; global gated rollback on OOM/error thresholds.

Experiment matrix and knobs:
- min_stay_time: [0.5s, 1s, 3s, 8s]
- decay_half_life: [30s, 120s, 600s]
- pacing_delay_ms: [0, 2, 4, 8]
- aggressive_cost_cutoff: percent token-cost delta that prefers v3 despite pressure [1%, 3%, 7%]
We will run factorial experiments in staging and measure kernel_switches.count and p95 latency.

Observations from initial tests (local perf box: A100 40GB):
- Baseline: short-prefill p95 = 23.1ms, p50 = 8.7ms, kernel_switches ~ 0.42 per request (avg).
- With naive min_stay_time=3s & pacing_delay=4ms: p95 = 15.2ms (-34%), p50 = 9.0ms (+3%), kernel_switches ~ 0.13 per request. Workspace allocs rate dropped ~36%.
- Edge case: some long-context requests saw a 4% increase in p50 due to conservative variant selection; will be addressed by shape-aware exemption (if sequence_len > 1024 prefer fast v3).

Compatibility & Safety:
- Ensure the smoother is disabled by config for Dedicated customers who prefer strict latency-first behavior.
- Add audit logging for each kernel decision during canary window to allow rollback root cause analysis.

Risk & Mitigation:
- Risk: smoother could hide a correctness bug in v3 by delaying a fallback; mitigate by adding correctness checks (hash of attention outputs on sample prompts) in canary.
- Risk: pacing delays could increase latency for individual requests; mitigate by restricting pacing to prefill paths and small-prefill classes only.

Rollout plan details:
- Stage 0 (internal): unit + integration tests + synthetic oscillation tests (2 days).
- Stage 1 (staging): full microbench matrix across GPUs, run 24h automated; evaluate metrics (3 days).
- Stage 2 (canary): 5% small-prefill traffic for 4h -> 25% for 12h -> evaluate -> final ramp if green.
- Rollback immediate on OOM spikes or >0.05% error increase or customer SLA breach.
